title: Host-native workflow UX for Codex and Claude
summary: Project one canonical workflow/audit model through capability-negotiated PiP, agent, approval, dashboard/carousel, preview, and accessible fallback surfaces without granting host UI authority.

current_state.summary: Source-attributed immutable host capability snapshots, loop stages/waves/gates, measured token projection, durable isolated commands, target-bound review consent/sandboxes, and 14 KB bounded dashboard pages exist. Native persistent lifecycle, unified surface events, authenticated native approval receipts, deterministic 3–8 carousels, and governed integrated previews are not yet one cross-host contract.

alternatives.name: Canonical semantic model with negotiated host projectors
alternatives.description: One versioned snapshot/event model drives thin Claude/Codex native projectors and fallback.

gains: Semantic parity and one audit authority
tradeoffs.revisit_when: All supported hosts implement one standardized native UI/receipt/preview protocol.

alternatives.name: Independent native implementations
alternatives.description: Each host reads workflow state and implements surfaces directly.

tradeoffs.revisit_when: Semantic host parity is explicitly removed.

alternatives.name: Enhanced bounded widget only
alternatives.description: Use HTML/widget and static artifacts on every host.

tradeoffs.revisit_when: Only as the fallback for unavailable native capabilities.

decision: Add host-neutral canonical surface snapshots and ordered events, extend source-attributed capability negotiation, and keep adapters transport-only. Use existing loop/review/command/token authorities; provide authenticated idempotent approval receipts, bounded deterministic dashboard pages, private disposable previews, and semantically equal fallbacks.

contracts.description: Persistent live PiP lifecycle with ordered bounded updates, truthful token provenance, reconnect, and terminal close.
Canonical stable agent/task/slot topology, wave/dependency, attention, state and outcome projection.
Context-rich <=2-action native decision surface and authenticated target/revision-bound idempotent receipt.
Semantically equal native components and deterministic 3–8-item carousel pages over lossless canonical datasets.
Authorized pinned private disposable sandbox plus browser/hosted/side-panel preview lifecycle with no push.
Source/confidence/freshness-bound per-surface selection and explicit accessible fallback without identical API assumptions.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC1: On every host profile supporting persistent PiP, one active workflow opens one session showing workflow identity, stage, active/completed work, attention, and last update; ordered changes are reflected and the session closes automatically on completion, cancellation, or failure, while completed static work never opens PiP.
acceptance_map.validation: Lifecycle matrix across Codex/Claude profiles asserts one live open, ordered updates, no static open, reconnect, and exactly one close for all terminal states.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC2: Complete, incremental, delayed, absent, malformed, and cross-provider usage fixtures show observed raw/effective tokens with scope/source or explicit partial/unavailable status, reconcile to the canonical token record, and never fabricate zero or estimates.
acceptance_map.validation: Seven usage fixtures reconcile value/status/source to runtime_eval canonical token record and reject fabricated zero/estimated-observed values.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC3: Serial, parallel, mixed-wave, retry, cancellation, failure, and resume fixtures visualize every dispatched agent with stable task/slot identity, role, scope, relationship, state, attention, and outcome matching the canonical audit record without duplicates or phantoms.
acceptance_map.validation: Seven topology fixtures compare stable node/edge/event sets to loop audit and assert no duplicate/phantom ids.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC4: Plan, design, dynamic-validation, review, and signoff approval fixtures show the exact decision, reason, target/revision, relevant evidence, consequences, owner, and approvability, with at most two primary inline actions and richer content moved to detail/fullscreen.
acceptance_map.validation: Five gate fixtures assert every context field, <=2 primary actions, and rich evidence only in detail/fullscreen with composer retained.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC5: A native approval advances state exactly once only when an authenticated human receipt is bound to the current decision, actor, target, and revision; stale, duplicate, replayed, disabled, unauthenticated, wrong-revision, or presentation-only actions cannot advance.
acceptance_map.validation: Positive receipt advances once; seven negative receipt fixtures produce zero transitions and explicit audit rejection.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC6: Canonical workflow, DoR, dependency/impact, agents, lenses, criteria, findings, validation, artifacts, and gate snapshots project on Codex and Claude with equal values, ordering semantics, provenance, and actions despite allowed host-specific styling.
acceptance_map.validation: Ten-component cross-host golden strips styling metadata and asserts semantic JSON equality, stable ordering/provenance/actions.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC7: Dataset fixtures containing 0, 1, 3, 8, 9, 120, and multi-page items use deterministic 3-to-8-item visually consistent carousel pages where needed, expose concise metadata plus total/current position, support navigation/filtering, and preserve every stable item identity.
acceptance_map.validation: Seven dataset fixtures assert deterministic page membership (3–8 where carousel applies), identical item-id round trip, positions, filter and navigation state.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC8: Inline structure and viewport tests prove cards are single-purpose, responsive, have no nested scrolling/deep navigation, preserve the conversational composer, respect the two-primary-action limit, and use detail/fullscreen for rich multi-step exploration.
acceptance_map.validation: DOM/structure suite at small/large viewports rejects nested scroll/deep navigation/>2 primary actions and asserts focus/composer/fullscreen behavior.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC9: One authorized design, build, and dynamic-review scenario opens an interactive pinned working preview in the host-integrated browser or side panel where supported, records preview identity/lifecycle, and links observed behavior to canonical evidence.
acceptance_map.validation: Three end-to-end flow fixtures authorize, open, interact, observe, evidence-bind and close pinned browser/side-panel previews.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC10: Valid, unavailable, denied, build-failed, timeout, attempted-push, escaped-path, external-network, and teardown preview fixtures prove execution occurs only in a registered pinned bounded disposable scope, never pushes or changes the source checkout/remotes, and fails safely with auditable outcomes.
acceptance_map.validation: Nine fault fixtures assert registered disposable identity, resource/network policy, push count zero, unchanged checkout/remotes, bounded teardown and named audit outcome.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC11: Supported, unsupported, partial, unknown, stale, contradictory, and changed-mid-run capability profiles record host/version, source/confidence, selected surface, limitations, and fallback and select deterministic behavior without false support.
acceptance_map.validation: Seven-profile matrix on both hosts asserts all provenance/selection fields and deterministic fallback for every non-supported or changed state.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC12: Disabling PiP, visualization, carousel, approval, sandbox, hosting, browser, and side-panel capabilities independently preserves canonical values, evidence, audit, gates, and reachable safe actions in an accessible bounded fallback that names unavailable rather than user-declined.
acceptance_map.validation: Eight independent disablement fixtures compare canonical fingerprints/gates/actions to native case and assert explicit unavailable labels and <=14KB fallback pages.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC13: Automated accessibility, keyboard, text-scaling, reduced-motion, light/dark theme, and responsive viewport checks prove native/fallback surfaces use system tokens/fonts/layout, WCAG AA contrast, semantic labels, alt text, visible focus, and non-color status cues.
acceptance_map.validation: Automated a11y suite across both projectors/fallback tests keyboard, 200% text, reduced motion, themes, viewports, AA contrast, labels/alt/focus/non-color cues.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC14: Concurrent update, reconnect/resume, stale UI, duplicate event, host switch, and terminal-close fixtures prove PiP, fan-out, approvals, dashboards, carousels, previews, fallbacks, and artifacts reference one workflow/run, target, revision, task/slot identity, evidence, gate state, and ordered audit history.
acceptance_map.validation: Six concurrency/recovery fixtures assert one identity tuple/event order across all surfaces, idempotent acknowledgements, stale rejection and exactly-once terminal close.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC15: Existing non-native design, build, review, status, approval, and artifact golden scenarios plus the native-capability matrix pass without lost evidence, weaker gates, removed tests, skips, xfails, loosened assertions, or reclassified failures.
acceptance_map.validation: Six legacy golden flows plus capability matrix pass; test-diff audit rejects removal, skip/xfail, lowered floor, loosened assertion, or failure reclassification.

risks.risk: Host UI becomes a competing workflow authority.
risks.mitigation: Persist canonical snapshot/event first; adapters emit receipts only; all transitions revalidate canonical identity.

risks.risk: Capabilities are inferred or become stale mid-run.
risks.mitigation: Source/confidence/freshness snapshot, explicit changed state, deterministic per-surface fallback.

risks.risk: High-frequency updates overwhelm host or duplicate model turns.
risks.mitigation: 4 Hz/16 KiB coalesced adapter queue; attention/terminal preserved; UI updates never wake model.

risks.risk: Approval actions replay or target wrong revision.
risks.mitigation: Authenticated actor/session/decision/target/revision/action nonce receipts with expiry and exactly-once audit key.

risks.risk: Preview escapes sandbox, pushes, leaks secrets, or remains public.
risks.mitigation: Registered private disposable scope, push-disabled adapter, path/network/resource enforcement, redaction and forced teardown.

risks.risk: Carousel/fallback hides data or becomes inaccessible.
risks.mitigation: Stable item-id round trip, deterministic 3–8 pages, lossless artifacts, WCAG/keyboard/focus tests.

failure_modes.mode: Capability is unknown, stale, contradictory, or changes.
failure_modes.detection: host_capability_selection reports source/confidence/freshness and selected/fallback surfaces.
failure_modes.recovery: Capability owner immediately switches only affected surface to bounded fallback; no canonical state changes.

failure_modes.mode: Native event is delayed, duplicated, out of order, or reconnects.
failure_modes.recovery: Session owner rejects stale/duplicate, replays from last ack, retries twice, then fallback.

failure_modes.mode: Token data is absent, malformed, delayed, or mismatched.
failure_modes.detection: host_token_projection reports observed status/source and reconciliation result.
failure_modes.recovery: Projection marks partial/unavailable and retains prior observed facts; never substitutes zero or estimate.

failure_modes.mode: Approval receipt is invalid or replayed.
failure_modes.recovery: Gate owner refuses transition, audits rejection, and refreshes current decision surface.

failure_modes.mode: Dashboard page loses/duplicates items or violates UI bounds.
failure_modes.detection: host_dashboard_page reports item ids, totals, bytes, action count and accessibility result.
failure_modes.recovery: Dashboard owner rejects native page and emits bounded artifact-backed fallback within two attempts.

failure_modes.mode: Preview build, isolation, network, push, or teardown fails.
failure_modes.detection: host_preview_lifecycle reports sandbox policy, pre/post source fingerprints, actions and teardown.
failure_modes.recovery: Preview owner stops process tree, revokes private endpoint, performs one forced cleanup, preserves source, and publishes failure evidence/fallback.

failure_modes.mode: PiP fails to close at terminal state.
failure_modes.detection: host_surface_session reports terminal event without close acknowledgement.
failure_modes.recovery: Session owner retries close twice, marks native surface failed, and shows terminal fallback without reopening PiP.

alerts: Fallback when surface update exceeds 16384 bytes or two retries.
Fallback when inline page exceeds 14000 bytes or carousel loses/duplicates ids.
Block gate transition on any invalid approval receipt.
Terminate preview on push, escape, unauthorized network, public exposure or resource bound.
Alert when terminal PiP or preview teardown lacks acknowledgement after retries.

rollout.strategy: Add canonical surface schema and audit-only projectors behind TASKPLANE_HOST_NATIVE_UX; enable capability/fallback, dashboard/fan-out, PiP/tokens, approval receipts, then preview runtime independently per capability. Dual-run Claude/Codex semantic goldens and retain legacy widgets/artifacts.
rollout.rollback: Disable new native sessions; close active PiP/private previews; retain event/receipt readers; project every canonical snapshot through legacy bounded accessible widgets/artifacts. Canonical workflow/audit data is unchanged and no migration is reversed.
